task_brief: Day 1 of "Interdisciplinary and Applied Design Practice" (unit 3, grade 11) is a diagnostic probe on cross-disciplinary collaboration methods. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 45–75 minutes. The unit is working toward: Deliver an applied interdisciplinary project meeting a stated brief with accessibility and stakeholder evidence. Today's work contributes to that by handling cross-disciplinary collaboration methods at the launch and diagnostic stage, against the unit's wider topics of cross-disciplinary collaboration methods, art joined with science mathematics or civic themes, applied and commercial design contexts, and client brief and stakeholder needs. This session is formative: it is scored on completeness and honesty of the record, not on getting a polished result.
primary_task: Before any instruction on cross-disciplinary collaboration methods, make a short baseline response so you can see your own starting point later. Spend a few minutes producing something — a quick sketch, a short pattern, a few bars, a rough plan, or a written description if you prefer not to produce a piece today. Then write three things you already notice about cross-disciplinary collaboration methods and one question you cannot yet answer. Keep this baseline; you will compare later work against it. Nothing here is judged for quality, only for being honest and complete. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about cross-disciplinary collaboration methods, and it belongs to "Interdisciplinary and Applied Design Practice", which also covers separate topics such as art joined with science mathematics or civic themes. Close out with this check before you stop: Name one thing you already understand about cross-disciplinary collaboration methods and one thing you want resolved by the end of the unit. At grade 11 the bar is independent work with sustained self-direction: you set the constraint, defend it, and revise on the evidence of your own checks rather than on being told to.
requirements: Meet this lesson's own success criteria: The learner completes the central task on cross-disciplinary collaboration methods., The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer., and The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.

Complete the critique criteria list in this package before submitting.
deliverable: Dated baseline response (made or described in writing), three noticings, and one open question, preserved for later comparison.
critique_criteria: A dated baseline response to cross-disciplinary collaboration methods exists and was made before any instruction.
Three specific noticings and one open question are recorded in writing.
The baseline is preserved for later comparison rather than discarded or overwritten.
A written description was accepted in place of a made piece if the student preferred; nothing required a camera, recording, or audience.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting cross-disciplinary collaboration methods.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for cross-disciplinary collaboration methods follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for cross-disciplinary collaboration methods, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to cross-disciplinary collaboration methods works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of cross-disciplinary collaboration methods, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking cross-disciplinary collaboration methods mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply cross-disciplinary collaboration methods under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on cross-disciplinary collaboration methods rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
